# Arca Kotlin SDK — AI Context

> com.github.arcaresearch:arca-kotlin-sdk — Kotlin/Android SDK for the Arca
> financial infrastructure platform (accounts, payments, perpetuals trading,
> real-time streaming, audit trails). Hand-written port of the Swift SDK; full
> feature parity. Targets JVM 1.8 bytecode (Android minSdk 24+).

```kotlin
// settings.gradle.kts: repositories { maven { url = uri("https://jitpack.io") } }
dependencies { implementation("com.github.arcaresearch:arca-kotlin-sdk:v0.1.0") }
```

Package is `network.arca.sdk`; the published Maven artifactId is `arca-sdk`.
Most calls are extension functions on the `Arca` class (`import network.arca.sdk.*`).

## Conventions (Kotlin-specific)

- Reads are `suspend` functions; mutations return a handle immediately (request runs in the background coroutine scope).
- Money/amount values are decimal strings ("50", "0.01").
- Market ids are canonical `{exchange}:{id}` ("hl:0:BTC", "hl:1:TSLA"), case-sensitive.
- Market-data timestamps are Unix epoch ms; all others are RFC 3339 UTC strings.
- Errors are a sealed `ArcaException`: Validation, Unauthorized, Forbidden, NotFound(code),
  Conflict(code), Internal, Exchange(code), Network(cause), Decoding(cause),
  NonJsonResponse(statusCode, body), OperationFailed(operation), Unknown(code). Branch with `when`.
- Order rejections: a venue refusal is `Conflict` (409) with code NO_LIQUIDITY (empty book — retry or
  use a marketable limit), MARKET_DELISTED, MARKET_NOT_TRADABLE, MARKET_NOT_USDC_COLLATERAL,
  VENUE_RATE_LIMITED (the account's venue request allowance is spent — on Hyperliquid it is earned by
  cumulative volume traded, not elapsed time, so waiting does not restore it), or
  ORDER_FAILED (refusal with no narrower code; verbatim venue reason in the message). None are
  retryable as-is. A bad-input refusal (tick size, price band, leverage cap, min notional, insufficient
  margin) is `Validation` (400) with the same verbatim reason. `Exchange` (502) means the request never
  got a verdict (connection reset, timeout, unparseable response) and IS retryable.
- Client-side only: authenticate with a scoped JWT (never embed an API key in an app).
- Always call `arca.close()` (e.g. ViewModel.onCleared) to tear down the socket + coroutine scope.
- Token-provider clients refresh ~30s before expiry, retry once on 401, and retry once on 403
  (`FORBIDDEN` / `REALM_SCOPE_MISMATCH` — cached token valid but minted for a different identity,
  e.g. after a signed-in-user switch; a 403-triggered refresh also forces the live WebSocket to
  reconnect). `onAuthError` fires when a 401/403 survives the refresh — tear down and rebuild.
- An `Arca` instance is bound to the identity its tokens are minted for: on identity change call
  `close()` and build a fresh instance with the new user's provider.

## Initialization

```kotlin
// Scoped JWT (realm read from claims)
val arca = Arca(token = jwt)
// With explicit realm + auto-refresh
val arca = Arca(token = jwt, realmId = "my-realm", tokenProvider = { fetchToken() })
// Provider only (suspend; fetches the first token now)
val arca = Arca.withTokenProvider(tokenProvider = { fetchToken() }, realmId = "my-realm")
```

## Operation & order handles

Mutations return `OperationHandle<R>` (HTTP runs in background):
- `submitted(): R`            — HTTP response before settlement (may be pending)
- `settled(): R` / `settle()` — suspends until terminal; throws ArcaException.OperationFailed on failed/expired
- `settled(timeoutSeconds: Double)` — throws ArcaException.Unknown("TIMEOUT") past the deadline

`placeOrder(...)` returns `OrderHandle` (wraps OperationHandle):
- `filled(timeoutSeconds = 30.0): SimOrderWithFills`
- `fills(timeoutSeconds = 300.0): Flow<SimFill>` — closes on terminal status
- `cancel(path)` / `resize(newSize, path)` (sized orders only)

## Intent -> method

| Intent | Method |
|---|---|
| Create wallet | arca.ensureDenominatedArca(ref) |
| Create any object | arca.ensureArca(ref, type) |
| Delete object | arca.ensureDeleted(ref, sweepTo?, liquidatePositions?) |
| Get object | arca.getObject(path) |
| Balances | arca.getBalances(id) / getBalancesByPath(path) |
| Transfer | arca.transfer(path, from, to, amount) |
| Move capital between two venues | arca.hopVenues(path, from, to, amount, sign) |
| Fund (dev) | arca.fundAccount(arcaRef, amount) |
| Withdraw (dev) | arca.defundAccount(arcaPath, amount) |
| Payment link | arca.createPaymentLink(type, arcaRef, amount) -> resp.paymentLink.url |
| Idempotency nonce | arca.nonce(path) |
| Aggregation | arca.getPathAggregation(path, asOf?) |
| Equity history | arca.getEquityHistory(path, from, to, points) |
| P&L history | arca.getPnlHistory(path, from, to, points) |
| Operation detail | arca.getOperation(id) |
| Create exchange | arca.ensurePerpsExchange(ref) |
| Place order | arca.placeOrder(path, objectId, market, side, orderType, size, price?, leverage?, ...) |
| Cancel / close | arca.cancelOrder(...) / arca.closePosition(...) |
| Position TP/SL | arca.setStopLoss / setTakeProfit / setPositionTpsl / clearPositionTpsl |
| Open with atomic bracket | arca.openWithBracket(...) -> entry + takeProfit?/stopLoss? handles |
| Exchange state | arca.getExchangeState(id) |
| Active asset data | arca.getActiveAssetData(objectId, market, ...); maxBuySize/maxSellSize include reversing and split as maxBuyReduceSize + maxBuyOpenSize (same for sell) — the reduce leg is never refused for balance, the open leg is what buying power gates. Null on Hyperliquid. |
| Set leverage / margin | arca.updateLeverage / updateIsolatedMargin / setMarginMode |
| Order limits | arca.getOrderLimits() -> OrderLimits(minOrderNotionalUsd = 10.0) |
| Min order size (UI gating) | arca.getMinOrderSize(market|marketId, price, reduceOnly?, isTrigger?, sizeToMax?) -> MinOrderSize(minSize, minNotionalUsd); ceil to szDecimals; treats any reduce-only as exempt — the venue only exempts an *exact* close, so verify a partial trim clears the floor yourself |
| Validate order size (advisory) | arca.validateOrderSize(market|marketId, price, size, ...) -> OrderSizeValidation(ok, minSize, minNotionalUsd, reason?) |
| Market meta | arca.getMarketMeta() / market(id) / resolveMarkets(symbol, opts) |
| Mids/tickers/book | arca.getMarketMids / getMarketTickers / getOrderBook |
| Projection registry | arca.upsertProjection(name, fields, resources) / getProjection / listProjections / deleteProjection — requires arca:ManageProjection; fields from the bounded catalog equity/realizedValue/unrealizedValue/positions; resources are path patterns ("/users/*") |
| Projection batched read | arca.getProjectionValuations(name, prefix?, path?, cursor?, limit?) -> ProjectionValuationsPage (keyset-paginated ProjectedValuation rows; only registered fields + identity are ever present) — requires arca:ReadProjection on the projection NAME |
| Candles | arca.getCandles(market, interval, options) |
| OI history | arca.getOIHistory(market, interval, options) -> OHLC open interest + 24h ntlVlm + mark; intervals 1m/5m/1h/1d |
| Funding history | arca.getFundingHistory(market, startTime?, endTime?) -> SETTLED funding observations {t, fundingRate, premium?, s?}; no interval (event series); default 7d, max 30d; HIP-3 supported; not predicted (use ticker funding/nextFundingTime) |

## Venue-to-venue hops

A transfer whose `from` AND `to` are both exchange objects is a **venue hop**: value goes venue-to-venue in one on-chain frame and never rests at a boundary, so no intermediate denominated arca is needed. Plain `transfer` performs it. Hops carry **no fee** (a non-zero one is refused, not ignored) and work across isolation boundaries. Destinations are limited to Hyperliquid and the paper venue; a GLL-paper target is refused because its account is faucet-credited rather than credited by value landing at the venue contract.

`hopVenues` is `transfer` **plus the co-sign fallback**, and is what to reach for when the source boundary might be armed. On an unarmed boundary it is exactly a transfer and `sign` is never invoked; on an armed one the plain call is refused (the kernel will not move value out unsigned) so it proposes, calls `sign(digest, proposal)`, and submits. `sign` is `suspend (String, VenueHopProposal) -> String` — a device prompt, a hardware wallet, a remote signer; the SDK never holds this key. Omit it and an armed boundary throws `ArcaException.CosignRequired`, whose `challenge` names `surface` / `boundaryId` / `propose` / `submit`.

`proposeVenueHop` (suspend) / `submitVenueHop` (handle) expose the halves when you want to drive it yourself. `path` is required at propose and must match at submit — the signed `ref` derives from it.

**`hopVenues` verifies the proposal before it calls `sign`, and so should you if you drive the halves yourself.** A digest is 32 opaque bytes: a key asked to sign one cannot tell a hop to your own paper account from a hop to a stranger's, and neither can a user staring at a device prompt. `proposal.verify()` re-derives the `paramsHash` and the EIP-712 digest from the proposal's own readable fields and throws unless both match what the server sent — so a propose response that quietly changed the destination sub-account or raised the amount is refused locally rather than discovered on chain. It also pins the EIP-712 domain to this SDK's own `ArcaCustodyKernel` / version `"2"` constants rather than trusting the response, so a signature cannot be moved onto a kernel whose semantics this SDK has never seen.

The pieces are exported for callers who want them directly: `Cosign.transferBetweenVenuesParamsHash`, `Cosign.operatorActionDigest`, `Cosign.domainSeparator`. Encode `amountRaw`, never the decimal `amount`. Keccak-256 is implemented in-package (`java.security.MessageDigest`'s SHA3-256 is NIST-padded and produces a different hash), so there is no crypto dependency to add. This SDK deliberately does **not** sign: `sign` stays yours, so the key can live in a keystore, a passkey-fronted enclave, or a remote signer. All derivations are pinned byte-for-byte against the Solidity implementation by the shared cross-SDK golden vectors.

## Watch streams (real-time)

Each factory opens the shared WebSocket and returns a stream exposing a `StateFlow`
snapshot + a `Flow` of `updates`; call `ready()` to suspend until the first snapshot
and `stop()` when done.

Snapshot-typed `updates` flows (prices, valuations, aggregation, exchange state,
max order size, equity/P&L/candle charts) replay the latest snapshot to collectors
that attach late, and drop intermediate snapshots for slow collectors (latest-only).
Event-typed `updates` flows (operations, balances, fills, funding, raw candles,
open-interest bars) do not replay; collect before mutating to observe every event.

Equity/P&L chart streams append an SDK-synthesized live tip derived from the live
aggregation (equity incl. unrealized P&L); it always carries
`status = ChartPointStatus.OPEN` so it can be identified (restyled / dropped /
re-anchored) without timestamp inference. Historical points come from the server
projection and carry the server's own status (`sealed`/`carried`/`incomplete`).

| Method | Snapshot / updates |
|---|---|
| arca.watchPrices() | StateFlow<Map<String,String>> prices |
| arca.watchObject(path) | StateFlow<ObjectValuation?> valuation |
| arca.watchObjects(paths) | StateFlow<Map<String,ObjectValuation>> valuations |
| arca.watchOperations(path) | Flow<Pair<Operation, RealmEvent>> |
| arca.watchExchangeState(id) | StateFlow<ExchangeState?> |
| arca.watchFills(id) | Flow<Pair<Fill, RealmEvent>> |
| — Fill trigger context | Fill.isTrigger (false = known regular order; null = unattributable — external trade/liquidation), Fill.tpsl "tp"\|"sl", Fill.triggerPx — decorated server-side, no per-fill order lookup needed. Liquidation fills carry Fill.liquidationKind "liquidation"\|"adl" (null on pre-stamp liquidations). |
| arca.watchFunding(id) | Flow<Pair<FundingPayment, EventEnvelope>> |
| arca.watchEquityChart(path, from, to) | StateFlow<List<EquityPoint>> + EquityChartUpdate |
| arca.watchPnlChart(path, from, to) | StateFlow<List<PnlPoint>> + PnlChartUpdate |
| arca.watchCandleChart(market, interval, ...) | StateFlow<List<Candle>> + CandleChartUpdate |
| arca.watchOI(coins, intervals) | Flow<OIEvent> (market, interval, bar, isClosed) |
| arca.watchMaxOrderSize(options) | StateFlow<ActiveAssetData?> |
| arca.watchProjection(name) | StateFlow<Map<String,ProjectedValuation>> valuations keyed by path — one batched watch over every object the projection covers. Loads the full initial snapshot (watch reply + REST pages), merges per-account DELTA frames (only changed rows arrive; a `removed` list drops deleted paths), re-marks rows client-side on every mids tick, and re-creates the server-side watch on reconnect/rotation. Requires arca:ReadProjection. |

Buying power is TWO numbers on a venue with a cross-dex reservation (the live
`hl` venue), not one. The venue-native dex (`hl:0:*`) keeps
`equity - totalMargin`; every HIP-3 dex shares a smaller pool,
`totalCollateral - reserved`, where
`reserved = max(marginNative, rate * notionalNative) + margin on other dexes`.
The `rate` floor applies to the **native dex only** — a HIP-3 position
contributes just its own margin, uniformly, on every dex. So only a *native*
position above `1/rate` (10x) separates the two numbers: the shared pool is
charged as if the native book had been opened at 10x. Below that they converge.

`ActiveAssetData.availability` carries both on every market
(`crossDexAvailableUsd`, `nativeAvailableUsd`, `reservationEnforced`,
`reservationRate`), so a ticket reading `$0` on `hl:1:NVDA` can also show the
larger native number instead of leaving a user to conclude their money vanished.
Not driving a live slider? `marketAvailability(exchangeState, market)` is a pure
helper (no network call) returning the same breakdown from a one-shot
`getExchangeState` — for a market list, a portfolio header, a static ticket.

```kotlin
val state = arca.getExchangeState(objectId)
val a = marketAvailability(state, "hl:1:NVDA")
```

The venue states the rule on `ExchangeState.collateralModel`
(`crossDexReservationEnforced`, `crossDexReservationRate`, `totalCollateralUsd`);
**absent means no reservation**. The `hl-sim` paper venue has a single pool and
declares nothing, even though it publishes the same `hl:<dex>:<symbol>` ids — so
one code path renders correctly on both venues, and turning it on for a venue is
a server config change that already-shipped clients follow. Don't show a single
account-wide "available" figure next to a market; the two numbers legitimately
disagree. A zero is never a "try smaller" — the venue refuses at any size, so
the remedy is a deposit (relief is exactly 1:1) or a smaller native position.
The reservation tracks *current* native notional, so it drifts as the native
market moves — don't cache it.

Knowing when an exchange arca can trade: creating one returns before its venue
account exists, and until it does every trading call answers 503
EXCHANGE_PROVISIONING. Two events replace polling for it.
`EventType.EXCHANGE_PROVISIONED` ("exchange.provisioned") means the venue
account exists and its metadata is stamped, so the object stops answering 503.
`EventType.EXCHANGE_READY` ("exchange.ready") means the trading agent is
registered on chain and it can actually trade. Both carry
`RealmEvent.exchange: ExchangeProvisioning?` (objectId, path, cosignRequired,
tradable, accountAddress, agentWalletId).

They are separate because on a cosign-armed boundary they are separate moments:
the account is provisioned, but its trading agent needs the user to co-sign a
grant, so provisioned arrives with `cosignRequired = true` and ready follows
only once that grant lands — minutes or days later. Treat the gap as waiting on
the user, not a stall. On an unarmed boundary both arrive together.

`EventType.DEPOSIT_DETECTED` ("deposit.detected") is money seen arriving at a
watched deposit address before it has been swept and become balance;
`RealmEvent.deposit: DetectedDeposit?` carries it. It is chain truth, not ledger
truth — `BALANCE_UPDATED` is still what says the funds landed.

Lower-level: `arca.ws` is the WebSocketManager (events flow, typed event flows,
onGap, onResume, onAuthenticated, onRotated, ensureConnected, disconnect).

`ws.onGap { missed -> }` fires on delivery loss, from either source: a hole
the client observed in the server-assigned deliverySeq (missed is exact), or
a server-sent `stream.resync` marker announcing that events were dropped
before they were sequenced — a loss no sequence check can see (missed is a
floor of 1). Both mean the same thing: refetch. Watch streams already do this
internally; register onGap only for state you track yourself.

**Sockets rotate before they are killed.** Infrastructure in front of the API
caps how long any WebSocket may stay open, and for a socket that cap is a
maximum lifetime, not an idle timeout — a perfectly busy connection is severed
on schedule. Reaching it costs an unplanned reconnect (backoff, TCP, TLS, auth,
resubscribe), during which a price display holds its last value and looks
frozen. The SDK therefore replaces the socket before the cap: a second
connection authenticates and re-issues every subscription while the current one
keeps streaming, and only takes over once the server confirms the new
subscriptions are live. Nothing is missed, no status change is emitted, and a
failure anywhere leaves the original socket serving. `connectionLifetimeMs` on
`Arca(...)` / `Arca.withTokenProvider(...)` overrides the 50-minute default, and
the server's reported lifetime is preferred over it when present, so the schedule
retunes without an SDK release. `0` disables rotation and outranks both,
including a server-reported cap, so the opt-out still works on the production
fleet — at the cost of an unplanned reconnect. `ws.rotateConnection()` triggers
one on demand and returns false when there is no healthy socket to hand off
from.

`ws.onRotated { }` (and `ws.rotatedStream`) fires when delivery has moved to a
new socket. This is **not** a reconnect — do not refetch history or run gap
recovery from it, since rotations are routine and a refetch there becomes
steady background load across every connected client. It exists for state the
server holds per-connection and so cannot survive the swap; the SDK re-issues
mids, candles, OI, path watches, and chart-history watches itself, and uses
this hook internally to re-create standalone aggregation watches.

`watchCandleChart` self-heals: it refetches recent candles on every WS re-auth
and app-foreground, and additionally detects seams in the live candle data
itself — a live candle whose bucket skips past the last held bucket, or a WS
deliverySeq gap, triggers a throttled refetch (10s cooldown, bounded to the
last 50 bars) of the affected window so server-side backfill corrections reach
already-open charts. The raw `watchCandles` flow is an unhealed event tap —
build charts on `watchCandleChart`.

## Anti-patterns

1. Reuse a nonce path on retry; do not call nonce() inside a retry loop.
2. Use canonical market ids ("hl:0:BTC", never "BTC"); resolve a display symbol via resolveMarkets(symbol).
3. fundAccount/defundAccount are dev-only; use createPaymentLink in production.
4. size is base-asset units, not USD. Min notional is $10.
5. Always close() the Arca instance (and stop() each watch) to release the socket + scope.

## Chart history is already marked; `points` is a ceiling

getEquityHistory and getPnlHistory are ONE computation — same buckets, same
marking; P&L history is equity history minus external flows. Every bucket's
equityUsd is that bucket's cash valued at that bucket's own mids PLUS
unrealized P&L on every position open at that bucket, valued at the same mids.
It is not settled equity carried forward and the marking is not limited to the
live point, so do NOT rebuild the curve from candles: a rebuild that projects
the CURRENT position backwards has no term for a closed position, a realized
loss, or a liquidation, and silently flat-lines the days before the newest
position. status describes the CASH side's provenance, not whether the point
was marked — CARRIED means no ledger event landed in that bucket, and such a
point still changes value as the market moves. INCOMPLETE is the degradation
signal (a mid was missing, or the position overlay could not run). Deposits
move equityUsd and never move pnlUsd, so chart equityUsd (present on PnlPoint
too) for "what is this account worth".

equityUsd is FLOORED at zero and the floor never destroys the number. Exchange
accounts are the one class permitted to hold a negative balance, and a negative
balance is worse to render than a zero. When the floor clamps a point the true
signed value comes back as unflooredEquityUsd; when it does not, that field is
null — so its presence is also the only way to tell a floored point from a
genuinely-zero one. pnlUsd is derived from the UNFLOORED value: a signed
performance delta must not be flattened by a balance clamp.

`points` is a CEILING: the ladder picks the finest rung whose bucket count fits
inside it, so a 24h window at points=180 is served at 15m (~96 points). The
response describes its own grid via resolution + bucketSeconds, with
resolutionRequested set only when coverage forced a promotion. Reconcile two
sources for the same series by window and resolution — never by "whichever has
more points", which a client-side reconstruction wins every time regardless of
correctness.

## TP/SL is an OCO bracket; openWithBracket is a linked normalTpsl bracket

setPositionTpsl stamps one auto-generated ocoGroupId on both legs; when either fills
(even partially) the venue cancels the other (cancelReason="sibling_filled"). A
setPositionTpsl / setStopLoss / setTakeProfit leg closes the WHOLE position by default
(sizeToMax, Hyperliquid positionTpsl); set a base-unit size for a reduce-only partial
(min-notional waived) — when sized, setPositionTpsl does NOT auto-link the legs.

openWithBracket(...) opens a position and attaches its reduce-only TP/SL triggers as a
linked normalTpsl bracket: one signature links the legs (NOT globally all-or-none — HL
only guarantees whole-payload rejection for pre-validation failures). normalTpsl is a
FIXED-SIZE parent-order bracket: each trigger child defaults to the ENTRY's size (NOT a
whole-position sizeToMax trigger); pass takeProfitSz/stopLossSz for a smaller
partial-close child. The trigger legs arm only when the entry fills; until then a child
is not a live venue order (no venue order id — addressable only by its cloid), its
handle matches fills by cloid, and cancelling it before activation cancels the parent
bracket. Returns one OrderHandle per leg.

## resize / modifyOrder on Hyperliquid is a cancel-replace

resize(newSize, path) treats newSize as the new TOTAL order size. On Hyperliquid this is
a cancel-replace: the venue cancels the old order id and places a replacement with a NEW
order id, retaining the cloid; the platform re-correlates later fills/cancels on the
replacement back to the original placement operation. newSize must exceed the
already-filled quantity (a resize at-or-below the filled amount is rejected). Unsized
(sizeToMax) whole-position triggers have no size to amend and are rejected.
